_about: NASA's Artemis III candidate landing regions near the lunar south pole. Each region is about 15 x 15 km; NASA has not published the region polygons in a form we could use, so data-pipeline/04_polar_illumination.py searches the area described below with LRO LOLA terrain and picks the best-lit, gentlest 2 km window inside it. The chosen point is Celestra's estimate, not NASA's site. Feature coordinates come from the IAU names (USGS Gazetteer, via Wikipedia) unless noted.

sources.list_2024: NASA, 'NASA Provides Update on Artemis III Moon Landing Regions' (Oct 2024): nine regions
sources.list_2022: NASA, 'NASA Identifies Candidate Regions for Landing Next Americans on Moon' (Aug 2022): thirteen regions
sources.mons_mouton_site: LPSC 2025 abstract 2742, landing site at 84.528 S, 30.719 E
sources.slater_plain: Wueller et al. 2026, JGR Planets, 10.1029/2025JE009434: Slater Plain about 20 km northeast of Slater crater

regions.name: Slater Plain
regions.feature: plain about 20 km from Slater crater

earlier_candidates._about: Existing Celestra targets that were Artemis III candidates in 2022 but are not on the October 2024 list of nine.
earlier_candidates.moon_shackleton_rim: Peak Near Shackleton (2022 list; not in the 2024 list)
earlier_candidates.moon_connecting_ridge: Connecting Ridge (2022 list; not in the 2024 list)
earlier_candidates.moon_faustini_rim: Faustini Rim A (2022 list; not in the 2024 list)

superseded.moon_malapert_massif: replaced by moon_a3_malapert_massif (Malapert Massif is on the 2024 list; the old point sat on the massif's flank)

relocate._about: Registry correction. These targets are named for a crater rim or ridge, but the registry used the crater-centre coordinates, which sit on the (often permanently shadowed) floor. They are moved to the best-lit, gentlest 2 km window on the named rim with the same search as the Artemis regions. Crater centres from the IAU names (via Wikipedia).

moon_connecting_ridge.feature: ridge between Shackleton and de Gerlache
